relationships.subject: TRPV1 intraepidermal nerve fibers
relationships.evidence_quote: Our study showed that ongoing burning pain is associated with an increased expression of intraepidermal TRPV1 fibers, as well as an increased dermal representation of CGRP fibers.

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: they also had increased CGRP dermal nerve fiber density compared with patients with painless polyneuropathy

key_findings: Patients with ongoing burning pain had higher TRPV1 intraepidermal fiber density and TRPV1/PGP9.5 ratio.
CGRP dermal fiber density was increased in these patients versus painless polyneuropathy.
